title: Internal audit and corrective-action closeout
body: A finding marked "Closed" on a memo means nothing if the CAR, the action guide, and the physical fix don't all say the same thing — Phase 1 at ADW had exactly that gap: a closure memo claiming all nine deviations closed while the working CAR still showed three open with blank evidence fields. If you sign off a closure report that the paperwork underneath doesn't support, you own that gap when someone checks.
keyPoints: A finding isn't closed until all four documents agree: checklist (what's wrong), CAR (the fix and owner), action guide (the evidence standard), closure report (verified close). One document saying "closed" while another still shows "open" is a live discrepancy, not a technicality.

Evidence beats a status label every time — before/after photos, signed inspection logs, toolbox-talk attendance registers. A row that says "CLOSED" with a placeholder instead of real evidence is not actually closed.

Physical safety fixes (electrical installation, emergency stop switches, signage) are the ones most likely to get marked closed on a deadline before the work is actually verified on the ground. Those are exactly the ones worth a walk-past, not a desk check.
Pair every open finding with its accountability owner — delineation findings go nowhere without knowing which department is responsible for maintaining them in each zone.
apply: Before you sign off any closeout — audit finding, NCR, or task feedback log item — walk the fix yourself rather than trusting the status column; the North Goline fuel area and haul-road signage are the two spots this KB's history shows get marked done on paper before they're actually done on site.
